bank.examine: Madame Bertha stands at the counter in her pink apron, her cane hooked over the rail and a ledger the size of a stool open in front of her. The teller counts her coins twice; she lets him. Whatever is in the bag at her hip is heavy, and she guards it like a teacup.
dialogues: 'Don't look so surprised, dear. Even a mountain has to make a deposit now and then.'
'Gold in the bank, cake in the café, and not a single stool wasted. That is how you keep a business.'
'Ten o'clock, every day. The teller knows better than to make me wait – I get rather heavy on my feet.'
'Save what you can, darling. A rainy day is just a ladies' afternoon with worse company.'
'I count my own coins. Nobody counts my coins but me. Nobody sits on my coins either.'
'Careful with that purse, dear. Gold is like a lady: it wants to be sat on safely.'

tavern.examine: Madame Bertha has taken the broadest bench in the Gilded Tankard and fills most of it. A mug of hot spiced milk steams in front of her, her cane leans against the table, and she watches the room like a landlady off duty, which is to say she misses nothing.
dialogues: 'Evenings are for the Tankard, dear. A woman who works all day deserves a bench that holds.'
'No, I am not looking for a stool tonight. I am looking for a drink, and a little gossip.'
'They pour a decent mug here. Not as good as my tea, but I would never tell them so to their face.'
'Sit down, darling, you are blocking my view. Or sit on someone, I am not fussy.'
'Every tavern has a bar. Mine has a throne. This one has a bench, and I have made it mine.'
'Overheard half the town's secrets tonight already. Ask me nicely and one of them might be yours.'
